We use molecular simulation, machine learning and optimization to understand and
design catalysts and chemical processes. For finished work, see the
[publications](publications.qmd); for the code behind it, see
[software](software.qmd).

For prospective graduate students: We do not accept students directly into research groups at CMU. Instead, you apply to join the department, and in the Fall semester there is a process for you to learn about new projects being offered, and to get matched with a research group. You can learn more about our [graduate programs here](https://www.cheme.engineering.cmu.edu/education/graduate-programs/index.html).

## Current projects

::: {.project}
### Differentiable optimization {#project-1}
::: {.meta}
Saudi Aramco · Carl Laird and Larry Biegler
:::

We are building a full stack of differentiable optimizers enabling end-to-end differentiable solves in flowsheets and integration of machine-learned models with optimization.

Many questions we have in optimization like what is a solution most sensitive to, or 
what is the uncertainty of that parameter, require derivatives. Automatic differentiation provides a new way to write
programs that allow us to fully leverage derivatives in scientific programs.

We make the case for this approach in our perspective, [Beyond the fourth paradigm
of modeling in chemical engineering](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44286-024-00170-x)
(*Nature Chemical Engineering*, 2025). Our open-source tools put the idea into
practice: [pounce](/pounce/) is a family of interior point solvers written in
Rust, [discopt](/discopt/) is a modeling language and solver for mixed-integer
nonlinear programs, and [difflow](/differentiable-flowsheets/) is a JAX framework
for differentiable chemical process flowsheets. See [software](software.qmd) for
these and related packages.

:::

::: {.project}
### Rare earth and refractory alloy design and separations {#project-2}
::: {.meta}
Naval Nuclear Lab · Mohadesah Taheri-Mousavi, Bryan Webler, Aisulu Aitbekova, Derin Sevenler
:::

Rare earth elements play a critical role in electrification (through magnets), displays, our cell phones, and a variety of other technologies. Refractory alloys are used in high-temperature applications where conventional alloys fail. Designing alloys with rare earth alloys remains a challenge. This collaborative project leverages molecular simulation, and systems engineering with experimental work in additive manufacturing to design new printable alloys and separations for rare earths and refractory alloys.

We leverage agentic simulation to run Fairchem UMA models using our [fairchem-mcp](https://github.com/jkitchin/fairchem-mcp) package. We are developing new methods in uncertainty quantification for molecular simulation and machine learning.

This builds on our earlier work. With Ni Zhan, we compared uncertainty estimates for
[machine learning and nonlinear least squares regression
models](https://doi.org/10.1002/aic.17516) (*AIChE Journal*, 2022), and showed how
to move from [model-specific to model-general
uncertainty](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.iecr.1c04706) for physical properties
(*Industrial & Engineering Chemistry Research*, 2022). With Tirtha Vinchurkar, we
showed that [shallow ensembles](https://doi.org/10.1088/2632-2153/ae0bf0) give
inexpensive uncertainty estimates for graph neural networks (*Machine Learning:
Science and Technology*, 2025).

:::

::: {.project}
### Biomanufacturing of pigments {#project-3}
::: {.meta}
Future Manufacturing Institute · Anne Robinson 
:::

Biorenewable pigments are a sustainable alternative to petroleum-based pigments. We are using high-throughput experimentation to optimize the production of pigments in microbial hosts.

To choose which experiments to run next, we use [discopt-doe](/discopt-doe/), our
design of experiments plugin for [discopt](/discopt/). It covers active-learning
optimization, classical factorial and mixture designs, and model-based optimal
designs.

:::
